text:
Systematic review and meta-analysis (PRISMA, PROSPERO CRD42023483105) of prospective randomized controlled trials comparing ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block (ESPB) against control interventions in pediatric surgery. Ten RCTs with 651 children were included after critical appraisal.

Technique. In ESPB, local anesthetic is injected into the plane deep to the erector spinae muscles (spinalis, longissimus, iliocostalis) and superficial to the transverse processes, achieving craniocaudal spread over several vertebral levels to reach the ventral and dorsal rami of the spinal nerves. In the included trials the local anesthetic dose ranged from 0.3 to 0.5 mL/kg, with varying agents and concentrations. Comparators: no-block analgesia (4 trials), caudal block (3 trials), quadratus lumborum block (2 trials), paravertebral block (1 trial). Surgeries were cardiothoracic (2 trials), abdominal (5), and hip (3).

Results versus no-block analgesia. ESPB significantly prolonged the time to first rescue analgesia (standardized mean difference 1.30, 95% CI 0.38 to 2.22, p=0.005) and reduced total postoperative opioid consumption at 24 hours (SMD -1.08, 95% CI -2.03 to -0.13, p=0.03). Pain scores were significantly lower at 4 hours (p=0.008) and 6 hours (p=0.0003) postoperatively compared with no block. No significant difference in pain scores at less than 2 hours (p=0.89) or at 12 hours (p=0.45), and no significant reduction in intraoperative fentanyl consumption (SMD -0.21, 95% CI -1.14 to 0.71, p=0.65).

Overall. ESPB improved postoperative analgesic efficacy in pediatric surgery, particularly against no-block or caudal comparators. The certainty of evidence was rated low to moderate by GRADE. The authors conclude that further high-quality, methodologically robust RCTs are required, and note that the mechanism and spread of local anesthetic after ESPB remain incompletely understood. Doses stated here are the range used across included trials (0.3-0.5 mL/kg), not a prescriptive recommendation; dosing follows weight, agent, concentration and local protocol.
title: Erector spinae plane block in pediatric surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
